subject: Compliance intake — DPA request, SCC module preference & role alignment
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@medicasys.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up from today's demo — DPA / SCC questions

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today — the platform looks promising for our triage workflows. A few compliance items came up on our side after the call that we'd like to capture and move forward on: 

- Can you confirm Redwood's SOC 2 status and whether you have an interim attestation or timeline to Type II?
- We need a DPA draft that identifies roles (controller/processor) clearly — our legal team prefers to start with a Redwood-as-processor template.
- For SCCs (EU transfers), which SCC module do you typically propose for a US-hosted processor serving an EU controller? If you can recommend an SCC variant that aligns with a processor role, that would be helpful.
- Finally, please send your vendor security questionnaire (or a link) so our security team can start a baseline review.

Would appreciate rough ETA for the DPA draft and the questionnaire link. We're aiming to have legal review complete within two weeks to hit our procurement window.

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of Procurement, MedicaSys

Hi Oliver — great to hear and thanks for the clear list. Quick summary & proposed next steps: 

Summary answers (short):
- SOC 2: Redwood has an ongoing SOC 2 program; we have an interim attestation summary (Type II expected Q4 2027). I attached the interim summary for context.
- DPA: We'll provide a Redwood-as-processor DPA draft (two options: minimal processor DPA, and an alternative with a limited subprocessor list clause).
- SCCs: For a US-based processor <> EU controller relationship we typically recommend the standard EU SCCs mapped for controller-to-processor transfers (Module 2 style mapping). I'll confirm exact module language with Karthik.
- VSQ: here's the vendor security questionnaire link — it pre-populates MedicaSys info and will let your security team upload docs: https://redwood.company/vsq/medicasys-7832

Proposed next steps (can we align on these?):
1) I’ll send the DPA draft and interim SOC 2 summary by EOD tomorrow (attached as drafts).
2) Karthik (cc'd) will provide recommended SCC module language and a short note on controller/processor role framing.
3) If that looks good, we can send the DPA into DocuSign and request legal redlines; I’ll include the HubSpot deal id for tracking.

If two weeks for legal review is your target, we can aim to have the DocuSign out within 48 hours of your review kickoff. Does that timeline work for you?

Thanks — attaching the interim SOC2 summary now.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Compliance intake — DPA request, SCC module preference & role alignment

Thanks for flagging, Lauren. A few points from privacy/legal side — recommended path to keep procurement moving: 

1) Roles: Redwood should be positioned as Processor; MedicaSys as Controller. This keeps standard obligations (data subject requests, lawful basis) with the controller while Redwood accepts processor-level safeguards and subprocessors. We'll include explicit language in the DPA.

2) SCCs: For transfers from the EU controller to a US-based processor, recommend the controller-to-processor clauses in the EU SCC framework (commonly implemented via the new SCC modules that map controller-to-processor obligations). I recommend we provide the customer a mapped excerpt rather than full SCC text (legal teams prefer a short mapping table + link to full SCCs).

3) DPA options: Provide two variants as Lauren mentioned —
   - Processor DPA (standard) — minimal, quick to sign.
   - Processor DPA + enhanced audit clause — adds quarterly audit rights and additional logging retention terms (for customers who insist on more oversight).

4) SOC2: note in the DPA that SOC 2 Type II is in progress and attach interim attestation; do not represent full Type II until the attestation is complete.

5) VSQ: recommend we trigger the questionnaire now. If they need faster answers on specific controls (encryption at rest, KMS, key management), we can provide short control extracts.

I’ll draft the SCC mapping blurb and a redline-friendly clause for the enhanced audit option and send by EOD. Keep external recipients limited to the two MedicaSys contacts until we have their legal team's preferred edits.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
